title: JAX: numerical functions to independent scientific work
summary: An offline CPU route through functional state, transformations, differentiation, training, scientific computing and measured systems tradeoffs, with explicit optional hardware boundaries.

lessons.title: From a Python function to a numerical contract
lessons.outcome: Specify a small computation and distinguish its numerical result from a model-quality claim.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the zero-weight predictor on the three observations.

lessons.title: Array axes, broadcasting and functional updates
lessons.outcome: Control the shape and meaning of every reduction and update in a small array calculation.
lessons.lab: Calculate row and column totals of [[0,1,2],[3,4,5]].

lessons.title: Dtypes, precision and numerical error contracts
lessons.outcome: Choose a precision policy and distinguish floating-point error from a wrong mathematical operation.
lessons.lab: Add one to 1e8 and subtract 1e8 using explicit float32, then float64.

lessons.title: Pure functions and explicit state transitions
lessons.outcome: Represent a changing computation as inputs and returned state that can be replayed and inspected.
lessons.lab: Apply observation 3 to the empty state and inspect both states.

lessons.title: Typed random keys and independent streams
lessons.outcome: Thread random keys explicitly and detect accidental reuse without claiming statistical independence from one sample.
lessons.lab: Draw twice from the same typed key with the same shape.
lessons.verification: Arrays agree exactly in this pinned process.

lessons.title: Pytrees organize parameters and state
lessons.outcome: Inspect, transform and reconstruct structured numerical state while preserving leaf identities and shapes.
lessons.lab: Subtract rate 0.1 times all-one gradient leaves.
lessons.verification: Every numerical parameter decreases by 0.1; old params remain unchanged.

lessons.title: Differentiate a scalar loss and audit one update
lessons.outcome: Derive a scalar gradient, compare it independently, and separate differentiation from parameter updating.
lessons.lab: Calculate loss and gradient at zero, apply rate 0.1, then recalculate loss.

lessons.title: JVPs and VJPs are shaped linear maps
lessons.outcome: Compute directional derivatives and pullbacks with explicit input/output shapes and an independent duality check.
lessons.lab: Compute a JVP at [2,0] in direction [3,4].

lessons.title: Jacobians, curvature and matrix-free products
lessons.outcome: Inspect second-order structure and calculate a Hessian-vector product without requiring a dense Hessian.
lessons.lab: Calculate the Hessian with jacfwd applied to grad.

lessons.title: JIT tracing, static inputs and compilation reuse
lessons.outcome: Predict which Python behavior happens during tracing and choose a valid compilation boundary.
lessons.lab: Compile repeat_add with n static and compare n=3 and n=4 for x=2.

lessons.title: Structured control flow and fixed-shape carries
lessons.outcome: Express dynamic decisions and repeated state transitions in forms compatible with the intended JAX transformations.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the recurrence on three values equal to two.

lessons.title: Vectorization, per-example gradients and axis meaning
lessons.outcome: Vectorize a scalar example computation while preserving shared parameters, sample identity and the chosen gradient reduction.
lessons.lab: Map predict_one over feature rows with weight [2,-1] shared.

lessons.title: Stable categorical losses and active-target masks
lessons.outcome: Compute a stable masked categorical objective and verify its value and direct logit gradients.
lessons.lab: Admit the fixture and compute its mean loss.

lessons.title: Optimizer updates are explicit state transitions
lessons.outcome: Implement and audit scalar optimizer transitions while distinguishing parameters from the state determining their next update.
lessons.lab: Apply gradient two at weight zero with velocity zero, then velocity one.

lessons.title: Train a small neural network with visible parameters
lessons.outcome: Assemble a bounded neural training experiment and distinguish optimization progress from evidence about new observations.
lessons.lab: Initialize the model and inspect parameter count and output shape.

lessons.title: Dropout, evaluation and stochastic objective contracts
lessons.outcome: Implement an explicit stochastic training transform and show why evaluation and replay require a declared mode/key policy.
lessons.lab: Apply training dropout with keep probability one half to ones.
lessons.verification: Every output is either zero or two.

lessons.title: Continuation requires parameters, history and keys
lessons.outcome: Define and verify a bounded continuation contract that preserves every state component used by the next update.
lessons.lab: Save the two-step state to an owned temporary file, load it and compare the next update with uninterrupted continuation.
lessons.verification: Matching next weight, velocity, key data and step count three.

lessons.title: Debug the first broken transformation invariant
lessons.outcome: Distinguish host conversion, dynamic shape and numerical-domain failures using bounded diagnostics.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the piecewise log extension and its summed gradient on [-1,0,2].

lessons.title: Linear solves, residuals and sensitivity
lessons.outcome: Solve and differentiate a small linear system while checking its numerical and mathematical assumptions independently.
lessons.lab: Solve the two-by-two system and reconstruct its right-hand side.

lessons.title: Differentiate a simulation and measure discretization error
lessons.outcome: Build a differentiable fixed-step simulation and distinguish the derivative of the discretized algorithm from the continuous model.
lessons.lab: Simulate rate one for ten steps over horizon one.

lessons.title: Monte Carlo estimates and pathwise sensitivity
lessons.outcome: Differentiate a fixed-sample reparameterized objective and separate that derivative from population expectations and Monte Carlo uncertainty.
lessons.lab: Calculate the sample objective and both parameter derivatives on noise [-1,1].

lessons.title: Custom JVP and VJP rule validation
lessons.outcome: Define and independently validate custom derivative rules while respecting their transformation limits.
lessons.lab: Evaluate softplus at zero and its JVP with tangent three.

lessons.title: Implicit differentiation depends on the solved equation
lessons.outcome: Validate an implicit linear-solve derivative by checking both the defining equation and its sensitivity assumptions.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the implicit solution at theta zero and multiply it by the diagonal.

lessons.title: Inspect shapes, jaxpr and compilation stages
lessons.outcome: Inspect distinct staging artifacts without treating their existence as a proof of portability or performance.
lessons.lab: Evaluate the abstract shape of gram on a (3,2) float64 input.

lessons.title: Benchmark completed work and separate its costs
lessons.outcome: Produce a bounded timing record that distinguishes compilation, warm execution and data placement without asserting a universal speedup.
lessons.lab: Time one first invocation and three later invocations of the same fresh jitted product.
lessons.verification: Correct products and two labeled timing groups; no required speed ordering.

lessons.title: Recomputation and donation change resource ownership
lessons.outcome: Preserve numerical behavior while reasoning about recomputation and the ownership contract of donated buffers.
lessons.lab: Compare cubic_sum and its checkpointed form on [1,2,3].

lessons.title: Array placement and sharding contracts on one CPU
lessons.outcome: Inspect real array placement and sharding metadata while keeping a single-device lesson distinct from multi-device performance.
lessons.lab: Put the host table into the declared row layout and inspect its addressable shard.
lessons.verification: Global shape (3,2), one CPU shard with the original values.

lessons.title: Collective mathematics and unequal shard counts
lessons.outcome: Validate collective reduction semantics on a named mapped CPU axis without confusing that model with physical distributed execution.
lessons.lab: Use the named mapped reduction on sums [2,12] and counts [1,3].

lessons.title: Port attention and low-rank updates by their equations
lessons.outcome: Reconstruct two small language-model mechanisms in JAX and compare values and gradients with independent shape-aware oracles.
lessons.lab: Admit the zero-score attention fixture and calculate its outputs.

lessons.title: Capstone: a checked differentiable numerical component
lessons.outcome: Deliver a small reusable numerical component with separate admission, mathematical, transformation and interpretation evidence.
lessons.lab: Admit and solve the unpenalized fixture, then evaluate its gradient.
lessons.verification: Weights [1,2], zero loss and zero gradient within tolerance.

lessons.title: Capstone: a reproducible training comparison
lessons.outcome: Complete a small training study whose data, optimization, comparison and limitations can be independently reconstructed.
lessons.lab: Train from zero for 400 updates and compare with the known coefficients.
lessons.verification: Coefficients within 0.01 of [1,2,-0.5], with reduced training loss.

lessons.title: Optional GPU and TPU execution qualification
lessons.outcome: Design and assess a device-specific qualification record without treating CPU or compiler evidence as accelerator acceptance.
lessons.lab: A hypothetical record says imports succeeded and one GPU was listed, but contains no allocation or output check. Decide what it establishes.
lessons.verification: Package/device discovery only; execution correctness remains unqualified.

lessons.title: Optional multi-host arrays and collective lifecycle
lessons.outcome: Specify a multi-process numerical and lifecycle contract with explicit ownership, data placement and failure evidence.
lessons.lab: Two hypothetical processes report loss sums 6 and 10 with counts 3 and 1. Define the global mean and required collective order.
lessons.verification: Global mean four, with both participants reducing sum and count in the same order.

lessons.title: Optional kernels, FFI and an independent engineering review
lessons.outcome: Decide when a lower-level extension is justified and specify the numerical, transformation and hardware evidence it must produce.
lessons.lab: A hypothetical affine GPU operator returns correct values for contiguous float32 inputs but has no backward or stride tests. Assess its status.
lessons.verification: One narrow forward case only; derivative, layout, dtype and broader execution remain unqualified.
